pr_title: Add support for Soma Tilt devices
pr_body:
## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->
Add support for Soma Tilt device.
Support for both Soma Shade was already fully functional but for the Soma Tilt device, this was only partially functional as it was not really implemented and was sharing the same functions and logic of the Shade device.
This PR introduce dedicated classes to distinguish Soma Shade and Soma Tilt devices, which make it now possible to implement different behavior for each one.
New releases have been published for the Soma Connect api to make this possible: 
- 2.2.5 introduce a flag to tell if the tilt device is closed upward or not
- 2.2.6 introduce the actual type of device (shade/tilt) in the list_devices endpoint

It implies that the full support of Soma Tilt is dependent on the Soma Connect API version 2.2.6 and above.
For versions lower than 2.2.6 (So if the type is reported by the API), the original behavior is kept and a Shade device is assumed, as there is no way to tell which type of device it is before this version.

issue_context.title: Soma Connect - Soma Tilt 2 doesn't react to tilt services
issue_context.body:
### The problem

Hello, 
I have setup a Soma Tilt 2 device (Along with Soma Connect) with venetian blinds. It is working perfectly from the smart shades app.
I then configured the soma integration in home assistant. My end goal will be to control the tilt position from a manual controller (e.g. Hue dimmer), and being able to set all the positions, from closed-down to closed-up.
I tested the integration through the service calls in dev tools. I can use with success all the services that doesn't contains the "_tilt" suffix. (open_cover, close_cover, set_cover_position). The problem with these is that they seems to be made for roller shades rather than tilt devices. For instance, when using the set_cover_position service, I can set the position from 0 to 100, 0 meaning fully closed down, and 100 meaning fully open. I can't set to position so that the blinds will be fully closed upward (Direct the light to the ceiling).
I then noticed that there was also services with the "_tilt" suffix. After reading the cover entity doc (https://developers.home-assistant.io/docs/core/entity/cover/), it looks that this should be the service to use for tilt devices as it states that "100 means open/maximum tilt". I tried to call these services but the device doesn't react to any services that contains the "_tilt" suffix (open_cover_tilt, close_cover_tilt, set_cover_tilt_position).
I enabled debug log for the integration but nothing appears (Error, warning, info, etc...) when calling these services.
I guess that these should work to enable the correct tilting functionality for this device, or is there something I'm missing?

Thank you for your help!

### What is version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

core-2021.3.3

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

_No response_

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant Container

### Integration causing the issue

Soma Connect

### Link to integration documentation on our website

https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/soma/

### Example YAML snippet

```yaml
Example generated from the "service" tab in dev tools.

service: cover.set_cover_tilt_position
target:
  entity_id: cover.tilt_bedroom
data:
  tilt_position: 80
```


### Anything in the logs that might be useful for us?

```txt
I tried setting the logs to debug for these components but nothing appears in the logs when I call the "set_cover_tilt_position" with the dev tools.

logger:
  default: info
  logs:
    homeassistant.components.cover: debug
    homeassistant.components.soma.cover: debug
    homeassistant.components.homekit: debug
```


Both Soma devices (Tilt2 and Soma Connect) are setup correctly and working perfectly from the Smart Shades app.
I tested with the Soma Connect integration and also with the homekit controller. The behavior is the same in both cases.
comments:
Hey there @ratsept, mind taking a look at this issue as its been labeled with an integration (`soma`) you are listed as a [codeowner](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/dev/CODEOWNERS#L443) for? Thanks!
<sub><sup>(message by CodeOwnersMention)</sup></sub>

Hey,

I think this may be because I never really implemented the *_tilt functions in this integration. I have to check with one of my colleagues about the Tilt support in Connect before I can say whether or not this would be an easy fix. At the moment the regular roller shade commands should also work for Tilt (other than the close direction I guess). There will be some magic necessary to map whatever HA uses for Tilt close direction (if it is even supported) to our implementation (-100 .. 0 .. 100 right now). We should also get better battery reading and also speed control in the next Connect release and I hope to implement Tilt functions then as well if nobody does it before that.

If anyone wants to try doing this they can contact me and I will help as much as possible. If not I can do this myself but it will likely be some time in the fall as we have a lot on our plate right now as it is.

Hey,
Thanks for your response, I understand why it is not working now.
I don't have a lot of free time but I would be happy to help implement this feature! 
That would be my first contribution to hass though. :)
I guess we first need an answer to confirm the tilt function is supported by soma connect as this integration simply interact with it right? 
When do you think you'll be able to get this confirmation?

Hey,

The Tilt is actually controlled by much the same functions as the regular shade and it does currently work (you can send -100 for close down, 0 for open and 100 for close up) but the readback of position always reports a positive number. I don't remember if I even used the value read back from the motor in HA but that should be the only thing actually wrong right now. The device type should already be reported correctly and the set position command will work with negative values. We just never thought it would be used like that but by lucky accident we also never implemented a check for the position command to always be positive. 

I will try to get an answer back in a day or two.

Ok great, so it sounds like it should be already supported by soma connect and only changes on the HA integration would be necessary. From what I understand, the tilt services in HA seems to only accept 0..100 values, as in 0% tilt to 100% tilt. So it should be possible to map the values to something like this : 0 to -100 (close down), 50 to 0 (fully open) and 100 to 100 (close up).
I'll setup a dev environment for HA and see if I can work something out! Let me know if you are able to do it faster :P
Thank you for your help :)

Hello @ratsept,
Just a quick update.
I did some tests and it turn out it should be simple to implement. I was able to confirm what you said about soma connect accepting values  -100 to 100 (though -100 is actually close up an 100 is close down). I still need to work a little more on it but I did implement the set_cover_tilt_position locally, with this logic:
- 0..49 in HA maps to the close down range for the api
- 50 is the middle point, and maps to 0 for the api (fully open)
- 51 to 100 in HA maps to the close up range for the api

Like I said, there is still some work to do, but it seems to work great like this. The only downside I can see is that not 100% of the possible positions can be used (100 possible positions for HA while there is 200 in the soma api), but in real world I don't see how this would be a problem.
Does this logic make sense for you? Any problem you see?

That should be fine. We do have a new logic for this in the next Connect release but I just talked with that developer and they said we are also keeping the current negative values for compatibility. Status messageges will report position values as always positive with a flag for direction. Move commands will also accept the positive position plus flag format.

I will try to set up a dev HA as well and if you get to a point where you can make a PR with these changes I hope I will also have time to look at it and test it. Thank you for spending your time on this.

Ok that's good to know!
Do you know when this next connect release is planned to be release?

Hey @ratsept,
I submitted a PR for this, if you have a chance to review it :)
I also check if I could do something about the broken current position reported by HA for the Tilt but with the data returned by the current api, there's not much we can do. Since the device seems to be only identified as a MAC address, I can't change the logic without breaking the Shades behavior. If the api could make a distinction in the type of device (Shades vs Tilt), it would be possible to implement 2 different logic to map the position back to HA.

I saw the PR but I also talked with my colleague and he said we should have a Connect update release in a day or two. That should fix some of the status feedback. But you can also already differentiate tilt from shades. The type of device is reported in the initial scan message and that could be cached by HA for each device.

Ok that's good for the type of device. I didn't see that yesterday but I honestly didn't spend a lot of time on it. With this info, it should not be difficult to implement. Since it's a different issue, it should also be in a different PR I think. I'll try to look into it as soon as I find the time :P
Regarding the new connect release vs this specific PR, I understand it will greatly help with the status feedback, and so with the current position in HA. Do you think the changes I propose in this PR are still valid or we should wait for this new release as there will be too many update necessary, event if it should be compatible with position -100..0..100?

I think what you have now will still be fine. Especially if it fixes the issue for you. Once your PR gets merged it will be possible to open another PR for the broken position feedback. 
I see that in the PR you also implement the tilt open/close functions and the close on that just uses one of the close directions hardcoded. I don't think that is ideal but I also don't see a good way of fixing this without actually changing the way HA handles cover entities which would be a huge undertaking. Maybe we will just add a configuration variable for the Connect to just swap the position direction. This would at least give the users a kind-of usable way of changing the default close direction.
I've never used the HA tilt thing - does it change the graphics for the entity? Do the graphics display correctly with the 0..50..100 implementation?

I can confirm it fix the issue and make the integration for the tilt completetely usable via automations. I can now use full tilt range, and so create automation for manual controller, or whatever trigger that change blind's position.

The ui for the tilt is the same, probably because in the end, it is a cover entity as is the shade. Because of the position feedback problem, the ui is not more usable than before for the tilt. It would probably need this next fix for the position to be reported correctly to HA to work as intended.

For the open/close tilt functions, I tried to implement something else but like you, I didn't find a simple approach. It is not ideal but for now, I thought it was better than nothing to have these hardcoded values. I think it is also more consistent to use open_tilt/close_tilt on the tilt device.

Hey there @ratsept!
I have upgraded to the new connect version (2.2.5) and did some tests to see how the different types of device were reported by the Connect api. I am just digging to see how easy it would be to implement a more complete solution for the tilt to make the current position work in HA. (And maybe just supersede this PR with a new one if it is easy enough)
I have tested a couple of endpoints and I'm not seeing anything related to the type of devices. 
I have tested these endpoints:
-  /list_devices : This one returns an array of shades, containing the name and the mac for each one
- /get_shade_state/MAC : This one returns the position, mac and the new "closed_upward" switch
The other endpoints are more related to actions so I didn't test them.

Is there something I am missing? Maybe another endpoint?
Can you clarify how I can differentiate tilt and shade devices?

Thank you again for your help :)

I just checked this and you are right. I'm sorry I mislead you with that - I was so sure we already implemented that. Our communications between Connect and our own backend use very similar data structures and there we have the device type as well. I have just talked to the team about this and I hope we can easily add this to the /list_devices response. If you think there is a better way of doing this let me know as son as possible. Otherwise I will try to make sure we get a new update in a few days with this added.
Do you actually have both devices (shade and tilt)? If not I could send you one quickly so that you could more easily test with both to make sure this is not breaking anything with the shade device type.

No problem!
Adding this to the /list_devices response seems like the best place for this. Having a quick Connect update on this would be great!
I currently have only a Tilt device, but I did ordered 2 shades devices on march 31. I guess they should get shipped soon. 
I'll make sure to test both devices when I'll have them.
The new version should now be public. I haven't tested it myself but this fix was really very small so I'm fairly confident it will do what is't supposed to.

Ok great, thanks for releasing it so quickly!
I'll test it out later today.
And also, just a quick status. I started working on a more complete implementation for the tilt yesterday. It's already pretty functional with the 2.2.5 connect version. The position is now correctly reported, tilt functions are working correctly, as is the UI. The only thing missing now is the new feature in the api to differentiate tilt/shade devices, which should now be functional with 2.2.6! I'm pretty close to be ready for a new pr.
I'll still wait for my shades device to be shipped to test with both types.

Can you contact me by email (tiit@wazombi.com) with your order  number so I can make sure it goes out as soon as possible? I'm not sure why it has taken so long to ship out your order but I really hope I can ship it out on Monday.

Hey @ratsept, just a quick note to let you know I tested and updated my code with the new 2.2.6 connect release and it works perfectly with my tilt device. I'll test with the shades as soon as they arrive and I'll send a pr if everything work as expected!

Your order should also be on its way now. I think the 2.2.6 version of Connect should also fix a limitation tis HA integration had before with a large number of devices being installed at the same time causing stability issues. This was mostly caused by the HA integration using polling (I think it still is) and no buffering on the Connect. Ideally polling should be avoided if possible but I don't think I'm good enough with Python to figure out how to make that happen in HA. Or how the API should even be set up on the Connect for something like that. The embedded code running on the motors does have BLE notifications that actually only report when a parameter actually changes. But this requires a constant connection from the Connect which would block phones from talking directly to the motors. So right now I think this is good enough.

Yes it is. It should be there by the end of the week.
That's good news if it solves this issue! From what I saw, yes, it is still polling the api at a regular interval.
This change you are proposing to avoid polling is great, but seems like a very big refactoring of the solution, with could have impacts on more that just the HA integration. I also think that for now, having full support for both device type in HA is good enough. :P
I'll be able to test it with 3 devices, which I guess this is not a large enough number to trigger the instability issues. :P

Hey @ratsept,
I received my 2 shade devices yesterday. I have set them up and integrate them with HA via my custom Soma integration.
Overall it works great! I now have 1 Tilt device and 2 shade devices. Each device reports the correct type, actions and position. They all works correctly too with the lovelace UI, with different icons and action for tilt vs shade.
I had 2 problems though when integrating those 2 shades with HA, but I'm pretty sure they are more related to the Connect API than the integration itself. Maybe you'll be able to confirm:
1- Those 2 shades are located in the same room. So, at first, I have setup a group for them in the smart shade app. I then integrated them to HA and realize that this grouping feature is not exposed through the api, thus not functional from HA. All entities appeared correctly though. I then delete the group in the app and refreshed the entities in HA. For some reason, I was only able to control 1 of the 2 shades from HA (Both were functional in the app). I first thought it was related to my code but I then called directly the api endpoints in a browser and saw that the second shade device was always reporting the position 0, even if I was playing with it in the app. I then restarted my Connect device and after a couple of minutes, both were functional again... Maybe it is related to the fact that I first group them in the app, but I have no way to confirm...
2- Because the grouping feature is not available through the Connect API, I did an automation in HA that is calling the "set_position" service 2 times back to back, 1 for each device. At first it works great (With a small delay between the 2 shades action), but then one of the shade was sometime not physically reacting to the set_position command. When it happened, I saw the new position correctly reported in HA, but the device just didn't react. The next time, both were working ok. I suspect this might be because both calls arrives too fast on the API, which is sometimes rejecting/not completing 1 of the call. I have added a delay of 300ms between the 2 calls in my automation to test this theory and I had no faults since...

All in all in works great for both device in regard to the integration. I'll test them tomorrow again and I'll be able to submit a PR in the next days!
Thank you for your help!

Hey @ratsept,
Regarding the second point in my last comment, I was finally wrong. I did some more tests and when there is a shade that it is not responding to an api call, it is because I'm already connected to it via the app on my phone. I guess there can only be 1 connection at a time on a device.
Also, I have submitted my PR for the fix. Not sure if you are able to review it as you are the codeowner of this extension...
